### F-720 — A packet-shaped rejection hid a typed error from the caller

> _2026-11-11 · core/blong-mle · resolved_

An over-ceiling ask was refused correctly, but blong-dev call printed the raw MLE envelope instead
of the reason, and the reply said 500 where the realm declared 400. The client was innocent: the
envelope decrypted fine and contained an empty object. A temporary probe at the gateway's catch
showed the caught value was an Array with keys `[0, method]` — the dispatch error packet
`[error, $meta]` rethrown whole — so type and statusCode were undefined on what the gateway read,
the reply took the 500 default, and \_formatError built {} because none of the fields it copies
exist on an array. One path rethrows the packet this way and it is not yet known which. The gateway
now unwraps a packet before reading it (gatewayCaught.ts, with a test), and the same call answers
the typed message at 400. Worth finishing: find the path that rethrows the packet, so the guard is a
belt rather than the only fix, and note that busGateway re-raises a decrypted error with
Object.assign(new Error(), payload), which loses fields the same way when the payload is a packet.

the gateway unwraps the dispatch packet before formatting the error; a packet-shaped rejection no
longer loses type and statusCode
